output.title: When rounding becomes a workflow decision
output.body:
If “rounding claims” keeps coming up as a vague complaint, treat it as one bounded workflow decision instead of a general annoyance. The real question is not whether the numbers differ by a little. It is which recurring workflow asks you to compare two slightly different numbers and decide whether the gap matters.

Start with one place where this shows up: invoice rounding, currency conversion, timesheet variance, or an estimate-to-actual gap. Then draw the control boundary. Which cases are already policy, such as rounding to the nearest cent? Which cases need human judgment, such as gaps above your own threshold? Which cases have no rule yet? If the difference is invisible and acceptable, it can stay in the background. If it affects approval or an audit note, it needs a clear human step.

The practical next step is simple: write one rule in plain English for one recurring workflow. For example: “round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” Then ask yourself one diagnostic question: do I already document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly, fix the policy first. The machine can wait; the paperwork usually does not.
